sentence: This project sets up a shared resource that helps analyze transcriptomic data and images of neutrophils.
This project studies how brain circuits in the fruit fly antenna help control movement in response to sensory information.
This project studies how specialized cells of the vasculature help stem cells move into the bone marrow.
This project measures clonal hematopoiesis over time in study participants to find its risk factors and whether it predicts age-related diseases.
This project combines chemical genetics with precision genome editing to find out how small molecules and proteins work.
This project builds mouse models of late-onset Alzheimer’s disease and studies them in depth so researchers can test treatments.
This project tries to find out how sodium-glucose transporter 2 inhibitors protect the heart, using cells derived from stem cells.
This project studies the neural circuits that control sleep behavior by looking for neurons in the brain that cause sleep.
This project builds a web-based computer model that predicts how well nanoparticles reach tumors in animals and humans.
This project studies how sphingosine-1-phosphate signaling changes the immune microenvironment in ovarian cancer.
This project studies brain-wide electrical network activity in mice under chronic social stress to find what makes the brain vulnerable to stress.
This project tests in mice whether natural killer cells help clear malaria parasites from the blood.
This project studies how disrupted signaling pathways relate to heart events in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, using transcriptomic profiling of myocardium and plasma.
This project studies how a piece of a potassium channel protein travels to the nucleus of heart cells and changes gene expression.
This project builds a bacteria-based system that delivers active natural products to targeted sites using engineered Lactococcus lactis.
This project studies planarian flatworms to find out how their stem cells stay resilient and keep regenerating.
This project builds a tool that matches organs to patients, aiming to improve transplant outcomes.
This project runs early phase trials that include ultra-rare genetic disorders.
This project tests a simple whole blood method to prepare patient samples for single cell RNA sequencing in sepsis studies.
